$comment: Every npm advisory this repository's trees carry, with the reason each one is still here.
scripts/dependency-advisory-gate.mjs reads this file and compares it against what `npm audit` reports
now, in both directions: an advisory that is not listed fails, and a listing the tree no longer
carries also fails. So this list cannot grow quietly and it cannot rot.
The gate is copied byte for byte into every repository that has one and checks its own body against a
declared sha256 on every run. This file is the only place a repository says anything about itself, so
an edit belongs here rather than in the gate.
THE PRODUCTION TREE IS NOT LISTED HERE AND CANNOT BE. There is no acknowledgement path for it at any
severity, and the gate refuses an entry below that turns up in the production tree.
productionTreeRule: The production dependencies here are @noble/curves, @noble/hashes and @noble/post-quantum and nothing else. They are bundled into public/app.js and they run in the operator's browser beside the key material, and SECURITY.md already treats an advisory against them as at least High regardless of its CVSS score, because a break there affects the integrity of every key the operator generates. No reason that could be written into a file would make carrying such an advisory acceptable, so no field is provided for writing one.

$comment: EMPTY, and that is a result rather than a default. On 2026-08-08 every tree in this repository was
taken to zero npm advisories by npm `overrides` that move a transitive package inside its own major
and leave wrangler, miniflare, workerd and @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers untouched, so the worker
runtime the tests and the deploy use did not change. `npm audit fix --force` proposes a different
trade, a major bump of @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers onto a miniflare 5 prerelease, and that was
refused: taking a prerelease worker runtime to close a build-tree advisory is a worse trade than
carrying it, and it would run the test pool on a different runtime from the deploy.
An entry here needs a package, a severity that matches what npm reports today, the version that
fixes it, whether a fix is REACHABLE from here, and a reason a reader can check. An entry whose fix
is reachable additionally needs a reviewBy date, and the gate FAILS once that date passes. That is
the difference between recording a decision and burying one. Before writing one, try an override:
that is what emptied this list, and `npm audit fix` does not try it.
What this repository's dependency channel does NOT see, named so that a green run is not read as
more than it is. This block is required: the gate fails if it is missing or if an entry carries no
reason, and it prints in full on every run whatever the verdict.
notCovered.github-security-api-channels: This gate reads none of GitHub's code scanning, secret scanning or Dependabot alert channels. Measured against the API for the public repository on 2026-09-25 rather than assumed: secret scanning and push protection are on, and code-scanning/analyses holds CodeQL, Semgrep and Scorecard results. Dependabot alerts answer 200 to a personal access token and are NOT read by this gate. The job it runs in is scoped to `contents: read`, which cannot reach dependabot/alerts at all: that endpoint needs the vulnerability-alerts grant. So reading them from here is a permissions decision rather than a line of code, and it is worth making: on 2026-08-08 a Dependabot alert naming a manifest_path was the only thing pointing at a second lockfile in the harness repository that no check in that repository audited.
notCovered.non-npm-ecosystems: npm audit reads package-lock.json, so it cannot see the GitHub Actions pins in .github/workflows, which Dependabot does watch. An advisory against a pinned action reaches this repository through a Dependabot pull request and through nothing else. The sibling website repository's website/scripts/security-posture-gate.mjs closes this by cross-checking the Dependabot alert list against what npm audit saw; that cross-check is deliberately not duplicated here, because it needs a credential decision in the job rather than a line of code.
notCovered.the-wider-website-gate: This gate answers one question, npm advisories in every lockfile in this repository, and it is copied byte for byte into console, engine and docs. The website repository does NOT carry a copy: its website/scripts/security-posture-gate.mjs already answers a strictly wider question over the same npm channel plus GitHub's code scanning, secret scanning, dependency review and Dependabot APIs, and a second gate beside it would be two instruments grading one channel. That is the one deliberate divergence in this family and it is written down here rather than left to be discovered.
notCovered.licences: Nothing here checks a dependency's licence. This gate reads severities. Licence review belongs to .github/workflows/dependency-review.yml, which runs on every pull request to main in the public repository and fails a pull request that adds a dependency under a licence outside its allow-licenses list. It reviews only the dependencies a pull request adds or changes, so a licence already in the tree is not checked again.
notCovered.coverage-of-the-build-tree-before-2026-0: Until 2026-08-08 the only dependency check in this repository was one line, `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`, which drops the build tree entirely. It was green while the build tree carried 17 advisories, 11 of them high.
notCovered.copy-parity-residue: Each copy also runs siblingReport (scripts/dependency-advisory-gate.mjs), which reads every sibling repository checked out next to this one and compares bytes directly, catching a pass that edited the body and reissued the digest in this repository alone -- when a sibling copy is present on disk to compare against. A GitHub Actions checkout is single-repository by construction, so a CI run here cannot see the other repositories and prints SKIPPED for each of them; only a workstation with the family checked out side by side (or a linked worktree under one) exercises the check for real. What remains uncaught: a coordinated edit landed on every repository's CI in the same push, before anyone next runs the self-test from a workstation that has the family checked out.
